reads_as_reason: A lumpy, bone-like clay form with a weak taper, no deliberate knee recess and a raw flat cut face at the shank top, though its surface is better than the baseline's.

G1.evidence: Near-constant-section sausage volumes; thigh pinches mid-length and re-flares above the knee; wobbly 3/4 outline and a lower-thigh dimple; P8a 0.788 and P8b 0.807 fail.

G2.evidence: Thigh ends in a round nose against a diagonal flat cut on the shank; bare flat disc with a seam line in the back view; knee reads as two stacked parts. Front silhouette more continuous than the baseline's.

G3.evidence: Colour not rendered; no clear groove at the knee to carry a dark tone.

G4.evidence: Similar front sections, but undulations (waist, dimple, calf bulge, ankle neck) read as separate lumps; end radii differ in side view.

G6.evidence: No references. Slab-like limbs and upper-third calf match; weak taper, wavy outline and missing knee cap do not.

pairwise.evidence: Baseline is a plain peg with a pinched waist and ledges at the knee, a bulbous shank and blotchy chaotic zebra. Candidate has a more continuous front outline, orderly concentric zebra bands and some intentional shaping; wobble and dimples keep it from sleek, so confidence is moderate.

top_changes.change: Increase taper; remove the mid-thigh pinch and lower-thigh re-flare: one monotone taper per segment.
Shaped shank-top cap instead of a raw flat cut; shared radius family at the knee so a dark recess can sit between.
Unify section squareness and radii; one calf swell, smooth stations elsewhere.

notes: Candidate = design-2 (Image B), baseline = design-1 (Image A). Contour lines in clay views may exaggerate lumpiness; zebra is the better surface test.
